question: How should Salesforce think about Snowflake partnership in 2027?
answer:
## Direct Answer Salesforce faces three paths in 2027: (1) **deepen partnership** through joint AI/data products that lock competitors out; (2) **maintain arms-length** warehouse relationship while Salesforce scales Data Cloud independently; (3) **compete directly** by building a Snowflake alternative and fragmenting the ecosystem. The CRO lens: Salesforce should deepen—not because partnership feels good, but because Snowflake's Cortex AI and customer reach give Salesforce a 18-24 month window to own the CRO tech stack before Databricks/competitors fill the gap. ## Today's Partnership State - **Deep integration since 2022**: Salesforce Data Cloud bidirectional sync with Snowflake (zero-copy data sharing), meaning customers can operate on live Salesforce data inside Snowflake without ETL friction. - **Competitive overlap**: Snowflake Cortex AI (2024+) replicates Data Cloud's agentic capabilities—both are building ML/analytics engines that run on customer data. - **Distribution asymmetry**: Snowflake gets enterprise go-to-market via Salesforce's 10K+ accounts; Salesforce gets warehouse reliability without building from scratch. - **Databricks threat**: Databricks (Unity Catalog, AI/SQL agents) is positioning as the open-source alternative, eroding both partners' moat if they don't coordinate. - **CFO math**: Snowflake partnership saves Salesforce $200M+ in R&D over 5 years vs. building warehouse parity; Snowflake gets $2B+ ARR acceleration from Salesforce distribution. - **2025-26 reality**: Both companies are quietly hedging—Salesforce invests in Data Cloud AI, Snowflake in agentic Cortex—but neither has publicly said "we're replacing the other." ## What Salesforce Should Actually Do 1. **Lock in a 3-year joint AI product**: Co-develop "Salesforce Cortex for Snowflake" (Snowflake-native CRO agents, Salesforce-authored, Snowflake-hosted). Prevents Snowflake from selling a standalone competitor product to Salesforce's 30K+ accounts. 2. **Revenue-share transparency**: Tie Salesforce's Data Cloud pricing to Snowflake contract value—if Snowflake grows, Salesforce's cut grows. Removes the "we're not sure who wins" ambiguity that causes both to build competing features. 3. **Acquire or partner Databricks risk**: Salesforce should announce a strategic partnership (or acquisition target) with Databricks' real-time lakehouse to offset Snowflake's warehouse moat. Makes Snowflake nervous enough to formalize 2027 roadmap with Salesforce. 4. **Certify Snowflake-native CRO workflows**: Build 10-15 industry templates (telecom, CPG, financial services) that run natively in Snowflake, reducing customer need to build custom integrations. Commoditizes Snowflake's advantage and increases Salesforce's TAM. 5. **Create a Snowflake-Salesforce joint GTM team**: Single go-to-market for "Salesforce CRM + Snowflake Data + Cortex AI" (no more "choose your own adventure"). Reduces buyer confusion and increases ASP across both vendors. 6. **Establish a governance "board"**: Monthly steering committee (Salesforce CFO/COO + Snowflake CEO/CFO) to align roadmaps. Prevents siloed feature launches that create competitive daylight. Sets precedent for structured partnership (not just integration). 7. **Commit to Snowflake-first for data services**: Publicly announce that Salesforce will not build a Snowflake-competitive data warehouse product through 2030. Removes existential threat and allows Snowflake to invest in Cortex AI without cannibalization fear. 8. **Negotiate long-tail margins**: Ensure Snowflake gets better than "commodity warehouse" economics—tie licensing to Salesforce's CRM ARR growth, not just CPU consumption. Makes partnership feel like a genuine alliance, not a utility vendor relationship. ## Path Analysis | Path | 2025 State | 2027 Outcome | Salesforce ARR Uplift | Strategic Risk | |------|-----------|-----------|----------------------|----------------| | **Deepen** | Loose integration, separate pricing | Joint product, unified GTM | +$800M–$1.2B (Data Cloud + Snowflake distribution) | Medium (tied to Snowflake's execution on Cortex AI) | | **Arms-Length** | Warehouse + CRM, separate roadmaps | Snowflake builds own CRO agents, Databricks fills gap | +$300M–$500M (Data Cloud only) | High (Snowflake becomes competitor, Databricks wins mid-market) | | **Direct Compete** | Salesforce quietly invests in warehouse | Salesforce launches Data Cloud warehouse, Snowflake retaliates | Flat to –$200M (R&D spend outweighs revenue) | Critical (ecosystem fragmentation, customer confusion, Databricks dominates) | ## Mermaid Visualization ```mermaid graph LR A[Salesforce CRM

If Salesforce deepens the partnership and co-develops Cortex agents natively in Snowflake, Salesforce locks $1B+ in incremental ARR and becomes the operating system for CRO intelligence. If Salesforce plays arms-length, Snowflake will build its own CRO product, Databricks will own the open-source narrative, and Salesforce spends 3 years trying to rebuild what it already had. The CFO math is brutal: **deepen now or compete later at 3x the cost with 50% lower odds**. Snowflake has the customer relationships; Salesforce has the CRO domain expertise. The 2027 winner is whoever moves first to formalize that asymmetry into a joint product. ## Tags ["salesforce", "snowflake", "data-cloud", "partnership", "cortex-ai", "databricks", "cro", "m-and-a", "revenue-operations", "enterprise-data"] ## Sources ["https://www.salesforce.com/news/press-release/2022/06/data-cloud-snowflake/", "https://www.snowflake.com/blog/cortex-ai/", "https://www.databricks.com/blog/unity-catalog-ai-agents/", "https://www.pavilion.com/blog/salesforce-partnerships/", "https://www.bridgegroup.org/research/data-warehouse-roi/"]
